history.howToUpdate: Append one entry to weeks after each execution cycle, then run 'npm run report:encryption'. Keep week numbers contiguous; the trajectory and per-feature tracker charts render placeholderWeeks empty columns ahead of the latest entry so the growth is visible.

weeks.label: W0
weeks.note: Baseline cycle. Full manual pass across all three templates; no automation in place yet.

plan.reusedFrom: The Purview auto-labeling harness in this repo: human-assisted sign-in with reused storage state, unique-subject correlation, polling instead of fixed sleeps, PASS/FAIL console plus JSON results, and automatic failure artifacts (helpers/outlook.ts, helpers/results.ts).
plan.scopeDecision: Web UI for OWA and Outlook.com, plus IMAP for Gmail and Yahoo transport assertions. Desktop clients (WODC Classic and WODC New) stay manual this cycle.

A.label: Runs on today's harness
A.surface: OWA to OWA, recipient in Prod, SDF or Outlook.com
A.currentStatus: All currently passing, so the value is regression protection over a large repetitive matrix.
assertions: Message is encrypted with the expected template (Encrypt Only / Do Not Forward / Internal Confidential)
Forward is disabled on Do Not Forward mail - guards a security control
All four attachments arrive with their original file names

B.label: Web plus IMAP
B.surface: OWA to OWA, recipient Gmail or Yahoo
B.currentStatus: Holds 58 of the 194 failures; the two dominant defect classes are MIME-level and therefore checkable without a browser.
assertions: Attachment file names preserved (covers the random-filename and missing-filename defects)
Attachment count and MIME types intact
B.staysManual: Attachment preview rendering inside Gmail and Yahoo web UIs.

C.label: Desktop, stays manual
C.surface: Any pair with WODC Classic or WODC New on either side
C.verdict: Out of scope for web automation
C.currentStatus: Both severe defects this cycle were found only here, so automation reduces matrix cost without replacing the desktop pass.
C.notes: WODC New is WebView2-based, so attaching over CDP is plausible but unproven. WODC Classic needs Windows UI automation (WinAppDriver or similar), which is a different toolchain and a separate decision.

phases.name: Harness extension
phases.work: Add encryption triggers (label, subject keywords ETRENCRYPTTEST / ETRDONOTFORWARDTEST / ETRINTERNALCONFIDENTIALTEST, and Options / default template), Reply / Reply All / Forward actions, the docx+pdf+xlsx+txt attachment fixture set, and assertion helpers for encryption applied, OME wrapper, forward-disabled and attachment names.
phases.unlocks: First end-to-end encryption scenario, same shape as the auto-labeling test.

phases.name: Tier A matrix runner
phases.work: One data-driven spec that iterates the combinations straight out of test-cases.json, so the matrix stays in data rather than in code.

phases.name: IMAP verifier
phases.work: Small IMAP module using app passwords to read the delivered message and assert transport-level properties for consumer recipients.

phases.name: Reporting loop
phases.work: Append each run's outcome to weekly-history.json so the trajectory and per-feature tracker update from real runs instead of hand edits.

risks: Consumer webmail actively resists browser automation, which is exactly why Gmail and Yahoo checks go over IMAP rather than through the UI.
Sessions expire; the harness falls back to human-assisted sign-in rather than storing credentials.
Attachment preview is inherently visual. Screenshot comparison is the only realistic automated form, and it is deferred.
The encryption templates and ETR subject keywords must stay stable, since the tests assert against them rather than creating them.
